resolution.statement: A dominant domain is the currently privileged interpretive domain in which a whole-expression realization is taken as the canonical reading because it yields the most direct organizational governance of admissibility, continuation, and residue without detaching subparts into independently primitive terms.
criteria: whole-expression preservation: the candidate domain keeps the expression intact rather than decomposing it into separately primitive parts
organizational directness: the candidate domain reads the expression directly in terms of organization, admissibility, continuation, and residue-conditioned progression
projection generativity: the candidate domain supports lawful downstream projections into other operator and application layers without requiring prior import from those layers
governance stability: the candidate domain minimizes ontological inflation and forbidden temporal-generator readings under current governance
resolution.canonical_status_of_AE: A|E is canonical at the current induction layer because it is the most direct governed organizational reading satisfying these criteria.
resolution.non_ontology_privilege_rule: Domain privilege is interpretive and governance-relative, not ontological privilege. Naming A|E as dominant does not make economics, physics, or any application domain foundational to the primitive process.
resolution.non_optionality_rule: A|E is not merely one optional paraphrase among many within this induction layer; it is the canonical dominant-domain realization currently used to stabilize whole-expression governance.

resolved_here: why A|E is canonical rather than optional
separation of domain privilege from ontology privilege
not_resolved_here: formal realization rule between (*|*) and A|E
